changes: Added from FAO DAD-IS (Polbar, Poland): cock 2.5 kg, hen 2 kg, cream egg shells, single comb and egg use. Confirmed the 1946 origin, Laura Kaufman's Green-legged Partridge by Plymouth Rock cross and the single conservation flock (about 1,000 to 1,100 birds) with both Wikipedia and DAD-IS. DAD-IS gives about 160 eggs a year as an average only, so no range was added. The new egg and weight facts rest on DAD-IS alone, so the record stays flagged.

summary.value: The Polbar is a Polish chicken bred between 1946 and 1954 by Laura Kaufman. She crossed the native Green-legged Partridge with Plymouth Rock roosters to bring in the barring gene, which makes the breed autosexing. At one day old, female chicks show a longer black stripe by the eye than males, so they can be sorted at hatch. Adult males are creamy white and hens grayish brown, with a single comb and gray to yellow legs. Roosters weigh about 5.5 pounds and hens about 4.4 pounds. Hens lay cream-colored eggs, around 160 a year on average. Today the whole breed lives in a single conservation flock of roughly 1,000 birds at the University of Life Sciences research station in Lublin, eastern Poland, so it is not something backyard keepers can easily find.
